standard_full: ASME B18.3 hexagon socket button head cap screws, inch series. The pages used cite ASME B18.3-2003 / 2003 (R2008) (aftfasteners, globalfastener), B18.3-1998 (nickel-systems) or ASME B18.3 without an edition (deltafastener, packerfastener, fullerfasteners); badensteel does not name the standard. All agree on every kept cell; values compared between public manufacturer / distributor pages only, not checked against the standard itself

shape_hint: Low domed (button) head with a hexagon socket in the top, flat bearing face under the head, fully threaded short shank; head diameter A about 1.75 x thread diameter, head height H about 0.53 x thread diameter. Hex key J is smaller than for a socket head cap screw of the same thread.

notes: Researcher notes (written before verification; where they differ, the clusters field and the verification field prevail). Clusters: US-A = aftfasteners + nickel-systems + packerfastener counted ONCE (same column set / labels; all three skip #5); deltafastener (own letters D/H/X/S/K/F, #0 - 5/8), badensteel (only C = hex socket and D = head height are defined by the drawing on the page; its 'A' pair is NOT counted), globalfastener 2003-edition page + fullerfasteners (one Chinese template), fasten.it (thread counts, A max, J decimal only: its 'H min' column holds the H max numbers), bayoucitybolt (socket size only). Thread counts additionally from general UNC/UNF charts. Tier B (amesweb calculator) carries the same values but is not counted. NOT used on purpose: boltport.com/standards/asme-b18.3/* and globalfastener 'ASME B18.3 (T11) 2012' reproduce the standard's notes verbatim (forbidden kind of source); the torqbolt 'button head' page shows the shoulder-screw table; fastenersuperstore / mscdirect / holo-krome / americanfastener sheets are PDFs; misumi and boltdepot answer with a bot challenge. deltafastener prints H min 0.055 for #5 where every other page has 0.058. Independence fingerprints: the AFT and Nickel tables differ from each other only in the fillet / length columns (not used) but share layout -> one cluster; Delta's table has different letters and a fillet-radius pair (0.010 / 0.005) the others do not have; Baden uses its own letters with a drawing; the globalfastener / Fuller template uses ISO-style symbols (dk, k, s, t). Left out although the numbers agree everywhere they appear: column J (fractional key size: only US-A and bayoucitybolt print fractions; amesweb [tier B] would be the third) and row #5 (A_min 0.226: Delta + CN; H_min 0.058: Baden + CN; amesweb [tier B] agrees with both; Baden's undefined 'A' pair also reads 0.238 / 0.226). Verifier (2026-11-11, fresh downloads, own parser): fasten.it is not counted; A_max and A_min stand on aftfasteners-group / Delta / globalfastener+Fuller, J_in on Delta / Baden / globalfastener+Fuller, H_max and H_min on those four clusters.

verification.checks_done: Verifier (different from the researcher) re-downloaded on 2026-11-11 with curl + browser User-Agent every counted page, all HTTP 200: aftfasteners socket-cap-screws page, nickel-systems button-cap, packerfastener button.html, deltafastener button page, badensteel socket-head-dimensions, globalfastener detail_1897, fullerfasteners button page, fasten.it asme_b18.3_table_3, bayoucitybolt, and the thread charts (engineeringtoolbox, runsom, echosupply, threadspec, trfastenings); eugenefast and amesweb fetched only to confirm they are HTML, not counted. Tables re-read with the verifier's own parser (researcher's raw files and scripts not used); drawings on the Baden, Delta, AFT, Nickel, globalfastener and fasten.it pages opened. 9 rows x 7 columns = 63 cells: A_max and A_min are stated exactly by 3 clusters (aftfasteners + nickel-systems + packerfastener / Delta / globalfastener + Fuller), J_in by 3 (Delta / Baden / globalfastener + Fuller), H_max and H_min by 4, thread counts by 3 manufacturer / distributor clusters (+ threadspec). Shared-typo test over all sizes each page lists: only Delta #5 H min 0.055 (others 0.058) and the fasten.it H column deviate, neither shared. Physical checks recomputed: A_max > A_min, H_max > H_min, A_max / H_max between 2.9 and 3.7, J_in < A_min, UNF > UNC, every dimension column non-decreasing. No PDF, document-sharing page, login page or page of standard text among the counted sources.
problems: Zero margin on three columns in every row: A_max and A_min rest on exactly aftfasteners-group / Delta / globalfastener + Fuller; J_in on exactly Delta / Baden / globalfastener + Fuller. Losing any one of these clusters empties the table.

Independence of Delta from the AFT / Nickel / Packer group (decisive for A_max and A_min): for the button head the Delta table is demonstrably a different transcription - letters D / H / X / S / K / F instead of A / H / S / J / T / F, a different drawing, rows #0 - #3 and #5 that the AFT group does not have, decimal socket sizes instead of fractions, a fillet max / min pair (0.010 / 0.005 ...) where the AFT group has the fillet transition diameter, and an own typo (#5 H min 0.055). No shared typo, no stated company link (Delta Fastener Corp., Houston; AFT Industries, Mansfield TX). Counted separately. Caveat: Delta's flat-head and set-screw pages reuse figures of the AFT / Nickel group, so the two sites do draw on overlapping material for other tables.

Baden: Table S3 has columns A max / min, C, D max / min, but the drawing on the page labels the head diameter B (not A), the hex socket C and the head height D. The A pair (0.213 / 0.201 ...) has no stated meaning and is not counted, although its numbers equal the record's A_max / A_min. C and D are accepted on the strength of the drawing. The page does not name ASME B18.3; the attribution of the values to the standard rests on the other clusters.

fasten.it asme_b18.3_table_3 is not counted for any column: its H min column prints the H min values for #0 and #1 (0.026, 0.033) and the H max values from #2 up (0.046 ... 0.331), and the #4 size label is garbled (4 (0.1129). A max and J hex socket agree with the record and would make A_max and J_in 4 clusters.
J_in: the AFT group and bayoucitybolt print the key size as fractions (1/16 ... 3/8); these are the same sizes but are not counted as exact matches of the 3-decimal values.
Edition: nickel-systems cites ASME B18.3-1998 for this table, aftfasteners and globalfastener 2003 / 2003 (R2008); all agree on the kept cells. standard_full corrected.
Thread counts: see ifhc - general UNC / UNF charts plus the globalfastener template; 3 manufacturer / distributor clusters, threadspec.org as a reference-only 4th.

Not checked: the standard itself. Row #5 and the fractional J column stay dropped as in the researcher's record (recount: #5 A_min 0.226 only Delta + globalfastener/Fuller; #5 H_min 0.058 Baden + globalfastener/Fuller, Delta 0.055).
